success_patterns: Compare the exact theorem conclusions: existence versus uniqueness, and a regularity exponent available for some parameter versus every parameter or the endpoint. Treat each stronger clause as a separate obligation.
Distinguish a separate witness for each order from one fixed witness that must realize every order. A rational algebra model alone does not establish integral realization.

patch.reasoning: The skill already emphasizes exact quantifiers and theorem matching. Clarifying the order-realization warning helps prevent conflating failure of a single common realization with failure of separate realizations, without asserting either conclusion without theorem support.

edits.target: a full-rank lattice order inside a rational algebra need not be ring-isomorphic to that algebra, so do not infer that one cohomology ring realizes every order.
edits.content: A full-rank lattice order inside a rational algebra need not be ring-isomorphic to that algebra, so do not infer that one cohomology ring realizes every order. Distinguish this common-witness claim from realizing each order by a separately chosen complex; failure of the former does not refute the latter, which still requires its own support.
